content:
When Apple finally responded to the surge in memory and other component costs, the company did not hold back. Some price hikes exceeded 50%, while memory and storage upgrades in certain cases effectively doubled in price.

These higher prices are likely to persist for years, and may even be permanent...

9to5Mac readers were already skeptical about whether Apple would bring prices back down once component shortages eased. Over two-thirds of respondents said they expected these price increases to be permanent.

A subsequent analyst report noted that supply chain prices would not see any improvement before 2028, and even then the improvement would be quite limited. The current high pricing policy appears set to remain for at least several years, and may never return to previous levels.

If this is indeed the case, how would you respond? Would you grit your teeth and continue purchasing Apple products at the same frequency? Would you reduce the number or frequency of Apple purchases? Or would you take other approaches, such as buying cheaper models, opting for refurbished units, or waiting for price drops?

Feel free to take part in our poll and share your thoughts in the comments. The poll allows multiple selections, in case you plan to change your spending habits in more than one way.
